target_customer: Special operations forces and other military and law enforcement units, buying through defense procurement
problem: Soldiers have to expose themselves to see threats in a firefight; existing AR headsets were too heavy, bulky and dim outdoors for combat use.
business_model: Hardware and software sold to defense customers, likely through government contracts and SBIR style programs (not confirmed by sources)

founders.name: Jake Bullock
education: Columbia University School of General Studies, class of 2017 (marked 17GS in Columbia's post)
founders.background_notes: Former Navy SEAL per YC page and Karl Guttag's July 2018 post. Columbia calls the company co-founded by him but names no other co-founder.

competitors.name: Microsoft HoloLens
competitors.what: Mixed reality headset that Microsoft was developing for military use; TechCrunch contrasts it with Ravn as focused on information during a fight

technical_complexity.rationale: A lightweight near eye display that works outdoors, takes video from guns and drones and survives combat needs optics, hardware and rugged engineering; Guttag's 2018 post notes existing headsets were wanting in size, weight, fit and outdoor brightness.

defensibility.rationale: Optics expertise from the chief science officer and defense procurement relationships are hard to copy, but large primes and Microsoft were pursuing the same market.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source states what incumbents did against Ravn; the Army pursued a large AR headset program with big vendors during the period, per search results not opened.

market_need_then: Defense AR was an active spending area in 2018 and 2019, and Guttag wrote in July 2018 that existing AR headsets were inadequate for military use; no spend figures were found.

branding.domain_note: ravn.com is now used by an unrelated custom software and AI engineering company, so the original company's domain history is unknown.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission focused defense language on the YC page

branding.community_and_virality: Named in TechCrunch's top 10 startups from YC W19 Demo Day 1.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand material found; name is confusable with Raven Resonance and the unrelated Ravn software firm that holds ravn.com.

outcome_analysis: Ravn had a clear founder market fit with a former Navy SEAL and a recognized optics expert and was named a top 10 startup of YC W19 Demo Day 1. No funding, contract, acquisition or shutdown has been found since 2019, and the original domain now belongs to another company, so its trajectory after the batch is not public.
notes: Company website ravn.com now shows an unrelated software company, so it is treated as not the startup's site. YC page lists Jake Bullock as founder; Guttag's post lists Blaine Bell as CTO, Paul Michalczuk as VP Hardware Engineering and Karl Guttag as Chief Science Officer, but none are called co-founders there, so only Bullock is listed. Two funding searches found no rounds; funding is unknown, not zero. Last dated material found is from 2019. Competitor list limited to the one rival with a source dated at the batch; Guttag's post names no competitors.
